purpose: Pinned build and test toolchain for foss-mcp on Windows. The binaries live in tools/ (git-ignored, about 8 GB). This file records what they are, where each came from, and how to restore it. Nothing here is a credential.
tools_root_note: Kept on C:, not in the OneDrive-synced repo. Override with the FOSS_MCP_TOOLS environment variable. relative_path below is relative to tools_root, except where it is an absolute C: or D: path.

tools.name: python
tools.source: https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3132/ (Windows embeddable or full installer, no admin needed for the zip layout)
tools.used_by: project venv (.venv), all ops/gatectl.py and pytest runs

tools.name: git
tools.used_by: every git call, and bash.exe for .githooks and scripts/ci_check.sh

tools.name: rustup-user
tools.source: https://win.rustup.rs/x86_64 (rustup-init, profile minimal, default toolchain stable)

tools.name: rp-toolchains
tools.version: see tools/rp-toolchains/TOOLCHAIN_PATHS.txt (ninja 1.13.2, winlibs GCC 16.2.0, LLVM 19.1.7, rustup cargo 1.98.1, typescript 5.9.3)
tools.source: Assembled by earlier sessions; each component's own source is recorded in TOOLCHAIN_PATHS.txt inside the folder.
tools.used_by: example verifier: ninja, cargo (cargo-home and rustup-home), tsc, and the GCC/Clang probes

tools.name: dotnet-sdk
tools.used_by: example verifier (dotnet platform). Already installed on C:; not copied into tools/.

tools.name: docker-desktop
tools.used_by: compose stack, live-content e2e tests, container build tests. Not portable; reinstall with the installer.

tools.name: visual-studio-2022-community
tools.used_by: MSVC link.exe and cl.exe for the Rust build and the cells/cpp verifier. The C++ workload is NOT installed on this machine (no VC\Tools\MSVC). Owner action: add the 'Desktop development with C++' workload.

tools.name: helm
tools.used_by: Helm chart lint and template tests (infra/helm)

not_restored_by_design: Build caches and downloaded packages (npm cache, cargo registry, pip cache)
Docker images and volumes (rebuilt by docker compose)
Any other project's tools, such as the actions-runner tree on D:

container_pins.note: What the Dockerfiles pin. tests/infra/test_container_pins.py enforces that each FROM digest, each ARG version default and each sha256 check equals these values. Every value was read from its official source on observed_on; nothing was typed from memory.

python:3.13-slim.source: docker buildx imagetools inspect python:3.13-slim (Docker Hub, read 2026-10-04)

rustup-init.artifact: rustup-init, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (the bytes are pinned; the file tracks the current rustup release)

dotnet-install.reason: Microsoft publishes no sha256 for dotnet-install.sh at an official URL that could be fetched on 2026-10-04, and no checksum was invented. The script also floats on channel 8.0. Owner or follow-up: pin it when an official checksum is available.

residual_risks: apt packages (git, curl, ca-certificates, build-essential, openjdk-21-jdk, maven) float with the Debian trixie mirror. They are not pinned to a snapshot date. Reason: a snapshot pin was not made in TC-174.
Java: the image uses Debian openjdk-21 (21.0.x). The host uses Temurin 21.0.11+10. They are different JDK builds and are not reconciled by this lock.
dotnet-install.sh is UNPINNED (see downloads.dotnet-install) and runs on channel 8.0 with a floating patch level.
The python base image is pinned to the linux/amd64 manifest digest. An arm64 build needs the index digest (index_digest) or a per-platform digest instead.

container_pins_observed.note: Host versus container pins. Each row must converge to host_lock. Until it does, reruns can differ by environment.
